utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody this morning. Mr. Registrar, can you call the case please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-83-T, the Prosecutor versus Rasim Delic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. May we have the appearances this morning starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours, Counsel, and everyone in and around the courtroom. For the Prosecution, Daryl Mundis and Aditya Menon, assisted by our case manager Alma Imamovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. For the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation] ... criminal defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, I didn't hear any interpretation. On what channel is the English channel?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Your Honours, the interpreters apologise. Maybe Ms. Vidovic can repeat the appearance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Would you please repeat the appearances, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. I am Vasvija Vidovic, with Nicholas David Robson, defending General Delic, assisted by our legal assistants, Lejla Gluhic and Asja Zujo, and we have with us Nina Kisic from the Criminal Defence Section of the Bosnia and Herzegovina State Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, madam.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before we proceed, Mr. Hamad, may I just remind you that before you started your testimony yesterday you made a declaration to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing else but the truth. You are reminded that you are still bound by that declaration today. Do you understand me? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Madam Vidovic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness. I hope that you rested well and that we can continue today.

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, we stopped at some questions that had to do with objectives of al-Qaeda in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and I would like to put some questions to you about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, can the witness look at D319.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And, Witness, before you look at this document, for the transcript I would like to say that it's an interview in the German daily Spiegle, Spiegle Online. Witness, can you please look at the interview. Do you recall giving this interview?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the Trial Chamber, I would like to explain that the original of the interview is in the German language, and the Defence has provided translations into English and Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I would like to pay attention to the Bosnian version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Did the Defence file the original in the German language? Thank you very --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I would like to ask you to look at the first page of the Bosnian version, the question before last. And in the English version it's at the end of the first page and the beginning of the second page. Witness, the question before last in the Spiegle Online interview you were asked about the al-Qaeda mission in the Bosnian war, and you replied: "Al-Qaeda wasn't interested in helping the Bosnian Muslims. They were interested in creating a base that would allow them to increase their area of operations, much like the USA with their bases but across the globe. Some leaders of the Western world noticed that but did not do anything." In relation to this, Witness, I want to ask you, did I understand properly that you felt that al-Qaeda in Bosnia was not interested in Muslims but in creating a base from which they could operate within Europe; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, now I would like to discuss with you your testimony where you describe your arrival in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And before that, Your Honours, I would just like to ask that this interview from Spiegle be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The interview from Spiegle is given -- is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 326.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to go back to that part of your testimony where you described your arrival in Bosnia and Herzegovina. You said that the members of al-Qaeda gave you precise instructions in Bahrain how to come and who to report to. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the instructions you received from Abu Helad [phoen], who was a member of al-Qaeda; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the second set of instructions. First I received the instructions from Prince Hamad and then from Abu Helad.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for that additional explanation. Now I would like you to look at Exhibit D320 -- or document 320. You have it in front of you. These are excerpts from your book, marked about numbers, and I would always like you to pay attention, please, Witness, to the high numbers, and this one is the number 06050396 and 0397. This is the second page. Please, can you look at this first page and look at line 7.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the English, Your Honours, it's also on the first page, beginning with line 6 and the words: "This is the number of the Sudanese who lives in Split."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I believe that you've had the opportunity to read it.

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It states here: "He gave me that piece of paper and said, 'This is the number of a Sudanese who lives in Split. When you arrive in Split, call him if you need help and you will be met by our people in a town called Travnik.'" Now, I would like you to look at the second page and then I will put my questions to you. On the second page can you please look at the sentence - it's around the middle of the page - which begins with the words: "They'll take you to the Mujahedin."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is page 2 in English. "They will take you to the Mujahedin," that part.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right, Witness. You've found it. I'm going to read from it. You wrote here: "These men were members of a Travnik Muslim unit called Muslimanske Snage, Muslim Forces. They're good guys. They love Islam, and they pray. When you arrive in the town where the headquarters of the Muslim forces unit is, you will tell them not to send you to a village called Mehurici where the Mujahedin training camp is located, but tell them to send you immediately to a village called Karaula and specifically to a village called Gradina. Our unit is billeted there." It's correct, isn't it, that here you are describing your conversation with Abu Helad. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you correctly describe what happened?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I described what I could remember, but most of my conversation with him is stated here in this excerpt.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. So you clearly wrote here that the instructions regarding the location of your unit in Central Bosnia was given to you by him, Abu Helad; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, in your testimony yesterday and answering to the Prosecutor's questions you said that Brigadier Asim explained where the locations of your units were. You said that he told you that one was in Mehurici and that the other was in Karaula. I would like to ask you this: Is it possible that because of the time that has passed since then you forgot the fact that Abu Helad actually explained that to you?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't forget that. I was told this in Bahrain, and I briefly said that everything was explained to me in Bahrain, where to go, who to report to, but I didn't speak in detail. My conversation with Abu Helad, I said that Brigadier Asim clarified things and told me where the Mujahedin camp was, where the front was, but this was his duty to explain that to me again. And besides that, he wasn't aware that this was already told to me in Bahrain.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: But do you agree that the instructions on the location of the units you already received from Abu Helad in Bahrain? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also received instructions to report to the Muslim forces; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And this is what happened?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And they accepted you, they welcomed you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if this number [as interpreted] can be given an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 327.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Testifying yesterday, Wahiuddin El Misri -- excuse me if I mispronounce the words.

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right. All right. No problem.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So Wahiuddin El Misri you described as the head of the Mujahedin in Bosnia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your book you describe them as well-known al-Qaeda figures; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, would it be fair to say that from your arrival in Bosnia and Herzegovina until you left to go to prison al-Qaeda actually decided your fate? Would that be a fair conclusion?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: My fate?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, your fate.

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't want to answer this because I'm not really quite clear about what you are trying to ask me.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will clarify my question. Is it correct that al-Qaeda decided about where you would go and decided that you would go to Bosnia, and then decided which unit you would join in Bosnia and so on and so forth until the point where you went to prison? Do you understand me now?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That is clear now.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you now please look at document D322?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the transcript, these are six pages of the book.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you recognise your handwriting; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you to look at the page marked a with the number 06050454. Can you look at the part in the middle of the page where your conversation with Wahiuddin El Misri is described.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is page 1 of the translation into English, and that part is at the bottom of the page and begins with the words -- and the words of that line begin: "Our unit in Bijelo Bucje has been left without suitable commanders."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, now I'm going to read the relevant section to you that I am interested in, and it states: "Our unit in Bijelo Bucje has been left without suitable commanders since Abu Talha El Andalusi was killed. I recently sent Abu El Ma'ali to lead the unit temporarily until you recover and get out of this clinic. Today you will be sent back there to take over the leadership of the unit from him." Would you agree that Wahiuddin El Misri actually appointed you as the unit commander?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like you to look at page 0650574 of the same document. Can you look at the part beginning from line 6. Look at the part that begins from line 6 on that page. Can you find it?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've found it. I have it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: "Our unit in Bijelo Bucje is left without suitable --" I'm sorry. We finished with that. I would like you to look at -- able I got a little bit of confusion. Can you please look at the page with the number 06050574. And there is a part -- Abu El Haris from the beginning is mentioned. He addressed Wahiuddin with the following words.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, in the English it's on page 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: "What do you think about Abu El Hasan El Mekki. Is he capable?" And Wahiuddin answered: "I think that he could be." And so on and so forth. "And then after that Abu El Haris then said to me: 'Listen, Abu Ubeyda [as interpreted], you'll go back to Bijelo Bucje and hand over the post of unit commander to Abu El Hasan. We'll inform him of this by Motorola. You'll be his deputy, and you'll be in charge of planning and executing military operations, because Abu El Hasan doesn't have much experience in this field. That's why you will always be by his side to assist him.'" And now I would like to ask you the following: It's correct, is it not, that Wahiuddin and Dr. Haris also decided that you would no longer be the commander but the deputy? Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Will you now look at page 06050591.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is it not so that they decided that he would be deputy as a result of him protesting and refusing to take the position of commander? There is that portion mentioned before the part that you read. Is it not so? What I'm trying to suggest is that --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What I'm trying to suggest is that he made a contribution towards that decision, and in fact that decision was in line with his desires. They wanted him to be commander, not deputy.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we first used the previous page at which by decision of Wahiuddin the witness was appointed commander. Then on the following page we see that the witness, by Wahiuddin's decision, was moved from that position to the position of deputy. And this is a relevant fact for the Defence, that is, who is the decision-maker about this, that's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I hear that, and that is why I'm saying that in fact that decision was made as a result of considering his contribution.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I accept that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have something to say, if I may. In this document that the Defence quoted from, that was the day when I was removed from duty. So as to avoid any confusion, allow me to explain. From the beginning of my tour of duty in Bosnia, when I was in Bijelo Bucje I was commander -- or, rather, deputy commander of the unit. After the attack on Ilijas in 1992 in which Abu Talha was killed, the commander of the unit, I became the commander by order of Wahiuddin. As for the document in which I described my conversation with Abu Haris, this happened almost five or six months later. So they came to fetch me in Bijelo Bucje and they interviewed me. They were not satisfied with my behaviour, and they came with intention of removing me from duties. They offered me to become deputy commander, which I refused. However, I was removed from duty. Of I was not commander or deputy commander then. This can be clearly seen if you were to continue to read on from this text.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may proceed, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, thank you for your additional explanations. Look now at this section on the same page, 060505911, and the part under title "Al-Qaeda decided -- took a decision about my arrest." Do you see that? And I will quote now. I think you can find this easily in the English version where towards the top of the page we see that: "Al-Qaeda has made the decision to arrest me," as he says. Allow me to quote this part of the text: "In the meantime, my al-Qaeda cell made a decision in connection with my case, the decision that was painful for me, because the al-Qaeda cell ordered the Mujahedin administration to arrest me." And in this connection, Witness, I wish to ask you the following: My understanding is that in Bosnia and Herzegovina there was an al-Qaeda cell. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you described that the decision was made by al-Qaeda with regard to your case; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So the Mujahedin administration ordered your arrest; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: They also decided that you should be arrested; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In this connection I wish you to look at page 06050599. There is a big title, "Military Court and 20-day Prison Sentence." I ask you, Witness, to look at the text beneath this heading. You mention Emad [as interpreted] El Misri here. You see that?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You described that in this case he played the role of a military judge.

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: On this basis my conclusion is that the Mujahedin had their own military court in Bosnia. They formed a military court of their own.

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Something that looked like a military court, but really one can't call it a military court.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because this happened in the Mujahedin camp before domestic and foreign Mujahedins. So this is my way of describing it. Any author describes things in his way, and that is how I described it here, as a military court.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me rephrase that question. Be that as it may, they decided about offences or lack of discipline which the Mujahedin; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now will you look at the last page of this document, number 06050680.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In English this is page -- the last page of this document, and the last two sentences on this page. And due to shortage of time I cannot discuss them with the witness, but they are relevant.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Have you seen those two sentences? You said that through an acquaintance from Bahrain you received a message from al-Qaeda: "From today on, you will be under Abu Zubeir in his unit where you will have absolutely no contact either with either Abu El Haris or with El Ketiba [phoen]." So will you please explain for Their Honours the following: Am I right if I believe that El Ketiba is the Arab word for the El Mujahedin Detachment? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Abu al Zubeir is quite a different Mujahedin unit in relation to El Ketiba or El Mujahedin. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But the same organisation formed El Ketiba and al Zubeir.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for the explanation, but my question is these are two completely separate units. Isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Finally, I am right in concluding on the basis of this section of the book that an al-Qaeda decided about your involvement in the al Zubeir Detachment. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, can this document be given an exhibit number and admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 328.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Ms. -- Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, reading through one of the documents a moment ago I noted that you describe the Mujahedin in Bosnia having something which you described as the administration. Could you please explain to Their Honours what the administration in Bosnia is?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what many people in Bosnia call Shura. That is the Mujahedin command which has its members, and they decide about all the needs of the Mujahedin in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I see.

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what the people in Bosnia refer to as Shura.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Will you now look at document D323, please. Again these are pages from your book. Will you please look at the page 06050462. I'm interested in the text beneath a heading, "Establishment of a Mujahedin Administration." Will you please look at it. Just this small section, and then I have a question for you. Is it true that Wahiuddin El Misri organised in Mehurici what you describe as a new Mujahedin administration which remained unchanged until the end of the war?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you please assist us. To the best of your recollection, when did this occur? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. Really, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was this when you were the commander in Bijelo Bucje? Was this then or before that?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Either -- I was either commander or I was removed from the command position.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was this before the events that you described yesterday? In connection with Guca Gora or after that?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid I can't remember just now. I need a little more time to think about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: If you remember, please tell us. But will you now look at page 3, 06050539. And again I'm interested in a small excerpt from that page. Actually, the last part of that page. You describe a conversation here with Wahiuddin again. Please look at that page. Am I right in saying that you're describing a conversation with Wahiuddin?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And towards of the end of the page you say Wahiuddin said to you, "That is why I wrote a positive report about you of which our bosses will be informed. This report will be sent somewhere where it will be kept and protected." In this connection, Witness, I should like to ask you it's true, isn't it, that you, the Mujahedin who were members of al-Qaeda -- you have already accepted that, haven't you, that you were observed by Wahiuddin and that he wrote reports about you to his bosses? Am I right?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So these are al-Qaeda bosses. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So it would be fair to say that the Mujahedin administration wrote reports about Mujahedin activities in Bosnia and their members to bosses outside Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Could this document be given an exhibit number, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, Exhibit number 329.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, let me ask you something else now. Testifying yesterday, you spoke about the fighting in which the Mujahedin took part in Bosnia and Herzegovina and in which you personally were involved. You remember that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your testimony with respect to the existence of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina remained unclear in my mind. When you were recounting the events of 1992 and the beginning of 1993, you said at the time the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina did not exist -- or, rather, there was no proper organisation in the army. Am I right in saying that?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: On the other hand, you claimed that the Mujahedin agreed or coordinated with army leaders regarding the battles at Jajce and Bijelo Bucje. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I add something?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, do.

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I mentioned that this happened before the BH army was formed. I called them army commanders before the formation and during the formation of the army.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What I would like you to clear up, how is it possible for army commanders to exist before the army itself was formed? I don't understand that.

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was my understanding here in Bosnia. I know that there was the TO at the time, which later was formed as the BH army. So I -- as far as I personally am concerned, I referred to them as the BH army even before the army was formed, because it was from these units that the BH army was established.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I see. And when did the BH army come into existence then, in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I noted that the BH army became better organised in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. In your testimony you mentioned Brigadier Asim. You mentioned him in connection with your meeting in September 1992 and then in connection with the events before mid-1993. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I say that in the BH army at the time there were no ranks, would you accept that? You always use the term "brigadier" when referring to Asim. However, if I put it to you that throughout the time period which you testified about yesterday, that is until mid-1993, there were no ranks in the army at all, would you accept that?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I explain that a little?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Give me a yes or no answer?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I don't agree fully with what you are saying, because it needs to be explained.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I called Asim the brigadier because he himself called himself a brigadier. I called Mehmed Alagic general because he called himself general before he became a general. So that is how I used those terms.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That explains your understanding of the events. Now let me also ask you about some other parts of your testimony. In your evidence yesterday about Bijelo Bucje, you said that Abdel Aziz told you that he had contact with Alija Izetbegovic and the military leadership with whom he had agreed where the Mujahedin would be billeted. Did I understand you correctly yesterday?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you did.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: First of all, my conclusion is that you knew Abdel Aziz well and that you were on good terms with him. You spoke to him.

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you tell Their Honours when Abdel Aziz left Bosnia and Herzegovina? I assume you know that.

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember when, but I know that he didn't stay for long. I remember that -- I remember him while we were in Karaula. When I was in Bijelo Bucje, he was no longer there. He had left Bosnia. So this means that he left Bosnia at the beginning of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, when then did he tell you that he had spoken to Izetbegovic about the billeting of the unit in Bijelo Bucje?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was when I had just arrived in Bosnia and when we were at Karaula. That is before we were accommodated in Bijelo Bucje.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So you're claiming that you learnt about this from Abdel Aziz; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In any event, you personally did not attend any conversation or agreement between Adele Aziz and President Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What is more, you don't know at all whether what Abdel Aziz told you was true.

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't. I referred to what he said.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And when we're talking about Abdel Aziz, it is true to say, isn't it, that he didn't control many different groups of Mujahedin in Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: But, Witness, let me go back for a moment to Alija Izetbegovic and Abdel Aziz. Do you agree that Alija Izetbegovic is a highly interesting personality, a central figure in Bosnia and Herzegovina? Am I right?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And Abdel Aziz was a leading figure among the Mujahedin. One of the leading figures.

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: On condition that you really did learn from Abdel Aziz that he had conversed with Alija Izetbegovic, because this is something you described in your book, because it's interesting --

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I described it because I believe that that is what happened. I wasn't personally present, but I believe it did happen, because this was confirmed -- this was confirmed by other Mujahedin, when talking to local and foreign Mujahedin. And before I came here in Bosnia, I saw pictures in Islamic journals of Izetbegovic, and the topic was the discussion between Izetbegovic and Abdel Aziz.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you agree that you gave a series of interviews to Glas Srpski or Glas Javnosti from Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And do you agree that you said there that you heard of Bosnia-Herzegovina for the first time when you arrived in Bosnia? That you knew about Yugoslavia, but not about Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course this was before we heard about the events in Bosnia. I was aware of this while I was in Bahrain, because the war had already started in Bosnia. Before that I was not aware of the existence of Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: But you now mention pictures of Alija Izetbegovic.

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Of I just wanted to tell you why I believe that Abdel Aziz did have a meeting with Izetbegovic, though I personally was not present.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I see. So you believe that this happened, but you do not know for sure.

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe and I'm sure, because I saw it in a journal in Bahrain. Unless this was a mounted photograph, but his picture was there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you more about the events that you described yesterday, the events related to Ilijas and Visoko. However, before that let me ask you the following: It is correct that the leadership of the Mujahedin planned their own actions in which they took part; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that they had their own organisation and that they requested that they should do their own reconnaissance.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. If you could possibly answer my questions I would appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: But still some of your questions require some elaboration. I cannot answer all your questions with yes or no without any further comment that I consider necessary.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. So you have explained it yesterday and also today. You said that they planned those actions. I'm now talking only about the planning. I'm not talking about any cooperation. I'm simply talking about planning.

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to refer to your statement given to the investigators. Yesterday you confirmed that you gave that statement in August 2006. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like you to take a look at D328.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm going to use D328 only to refresh the memory of the witness. It's page 71 of the transcript. Your Honours, in English it is the end of page 71 where it mentions the principal person, and then it goes on to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And to you, Witness, I'm going to quote the following: You said, "The principal person was a Wahiuddin El Misri. He was the military expert who had planned all attacks that were performed by the Mujahedin. He was one of the most important persons of al-Qaeda, and he was very operative while he was in Afghanistan. Another person is an Egyptian, also a very important man. His name is Ebu El Mu'utaz El Misri. He was one of the important persons among the Mujahedin forces in Bosnia during the war. He is a member of al-Qaeda. I know him from Afghanistan. We were there together." So, Witness, this is what I'm talking about. Is this correct what you have written in this part of your book?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, the boss of the Mujahedin would evaluate the circumstances related to actions and then himself made the decision about the participation of Mujahedins in these actions.

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: He would accept or not accept that they were participate in battles; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday you were telling us about some agreements with, as you put it, army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, agreements related to participation in battles. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, in actual fact during all the time that you spent on the position of the commander of the unit in Bijelo Bucje, you never received a single order from army of Bosnia and Herzegovina; is that correct? I'm talking about orders now. You personally never received an order from BH army?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not from them. There was only cooperation. There were no orders.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Specifically, you never received any written order?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like to show you again a document that the Prosecutor showed you yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What do you want to do with this one? Thank you very [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Document D328 is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 330.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like the witness to take a look at PT1024, and that's P121. Of it has already and admitted as P121. Here it has the number PT1024. Witness, you read this document yesterday, and I would like you to take a look at a small passage today. I'm interested in the second page of the document. The number is 10832730. Can you take a look at the passage which finishes with "El Hamdulila." After of that there are two more paragraphs some place above the middle of the page beginning with the words "Some of the Mujahedins."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it's on second page in English. Second page in English. I think this is okay. Beginning with "Some Mujahids."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I haven't found it. Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It begins with "Some Mujahids." Have you seen that?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have it now.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'll quote it. It says: "Some Mujahids, including Arabs, without my order moved towards elevation 744 on the right-hand side. Then they came down to the village and started torching. I caught up with two Mujahids and informed Emir Heldic [phoen] that he and the Mujahids should withdraw. However, the Arabs went even further to the right." Witness, do you agree that the author of this part of the report says that the Arabs went without his order towards elevation 744?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Wait a minute. Wait a minute. Now I'm talking about the report. I'm talking about the report, and then after that I'm going to ask you about your understanding of the situation. So my question is: Do you agree that the author of this report describes the situation in those words?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So he says that they went there without his control. He ordered the withdrawal, and they did something opposite. So now in relation to this I want to ask you the following: You maybe don't know all the details about this action. Am I correct about that?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are details that I'm not aware of, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday in your testimony you mentioned Ramo Durmis; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that he couldn't have ordered Mujahedins while taking part in this action? I'm talking about him.

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with that, because I was there and I was commanding. It means that he couldn't command Arabs. I don't agree with this part of his statement where he says that the Arabs were torching the village. It was done by the locals.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. All right. But I'm interested in this part. Thank you for your explanation, but this is what I'm interested in: "Ramo Durmis could not command them." Is that correct? I'm talking here about the Mujahedins.

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, now I would like to move on to another topic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now about Mehmed Alagic, or General Alagic. Yesterday in your testimony you referred to contacts with the army commanders, and you mostly spoke about Mehmed Alagic. You said that he was a general and the commander of the 7th Corps; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When talking about Mehmed Alagic, you established a connection between the agreement -- between him and the agreement between the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina and Mujahedin related to the fall of Jajce. Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you did.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that Jajce fell towards the end of 1992? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also established a connection between him and the agreements related to the attack on Ilijas. Did I understand that correctly?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: That is also the end of 1992.

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that he introduced himself as General Alagic.

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, if I now put forward the claim that Mehmed Alagic, until the middle of January 1993, until the middle of January 1993, he was not even in Bosnia and Herzegovina, would that change your opinion on his role?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would not. There is a simple reason for that. Can I explain that?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, you may.

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm still trying to tell you that it is very difficult for me to be specific about dates and periods of events, so it is possible that maybe sometimes I jump two or three months forward or backward, and I think I have made it very clear in my written statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that you established connection between him and a very specific event, the fall of Jajce and Ilijas? So you connect him with some events.

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So I have understood you correctly. Witness, I would now like to tell you that you, even when you were commander, that is in the first half of 1993, didn't really have the understanding about which corps of the BH army was covering Central Bosnia. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was told that the general of the 7th Corps was Mehmed Alagic. That's what I heard from him and from Brigadier Asim.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like the witness to take a look at the document. And also, Your Honour, I should tell you that you're supposed to take the second binder that we have given -- no, you're actually about to get it. I'm sorry. We were forced to reorganise our cross-examination yesterday. Also a copy for the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just a second, Madam Vidovic. Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The Prosecution simply wants to note for the record that this is the second time we've received with a witness significant additional documents on the second day of the cross-examination. A similar -- similar situation arose with respect to Witness PW-3, and pursuant to the guidelines it's our understanding that the Defence exhibits should be provided at the conclusion of the direct examination, whereas one or two additional documents present us with no problem. I just simply want to put on the record at this point that this is the second time -- second witness where we've received significant additional documents on the second day of the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Any comment, Madam Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Actually, the documents we received from the Prosecutor while preparing the testimony of this witness were substantially different from his testimony yesterday. We prepared our cross-examination based on the statements we received. Of the Prosecution changed his line of examination, and I really have to say that I'm not a magician. I simply couldn't possibly change and adapt my documents so quickly. We barely managed, Your Honours, to reorganise all this now. And the reason for that is the fact that the Prosecutor in his examination covered also other areas from the indictment. It simply means that I also had to refer to part of the testimony yesterday, and it caused me to change the line of my cross-examination. Anyway, Your Honour, you have to bear in mind that I really try to give the documents related to cross-examination in time, and I believe that the Prosecutor is going to find himself in the same situation when he will be the one to cross-examine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this point I'm certainly not objecting to the Defence proceeding. I simply wanted to put that on the record so that if we continue to have this situation then perhaps we can take additional further steps. But I -- but I do feel I must respond to the comments concerning the direct examination. I believe that if the Trial Chamber were to take a look at the 65 ter summary of the expected testimony of this witness, there are not significant or substantial deviations from the 65 ter statement or material 65 ter summary and the direct examination. But I don't want to take up any further time on this matter and suggest we proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Then the Chamber will not bother to look into the 65 ter list. We've understood that the matter is placed on the record. You may proceed, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, take a look at D332. For the record, it's an order dated 26th of February, 1994, which appoints Mehmed Alagic, son of Redzo. Witness, can you take a look at the second part of the document. Do you agree that the document is dated the 26th of February, 1994? Take a look at the second part of the document. "To the 7th Corps, Brigadier Mehmed Alagic, son of Redzo, to the post of corps commander. Until now in the post of the 3rd Corps commander."

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that this document says that Alagic not even in February 1994 was a general but only a brigadier? Do you see that in the document?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Also, he wasn't the commander of the 7th Corps at the time. Do you agree were that? You agree that that's what the document says?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not changing my testimony. It's the same, although I see the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, can we give the exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, Exhibit 331.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your testimony yesterday you said that the Mujahedins would observe the orders of Alagic, and that included yourself.

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And as an example, you said that Alagic told you not to blow up the church in Guca Gora.

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not quite. It was the chief of Mujahedins who accepted this order.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you about -- through for this explanation.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, maybe it would be better if we had a break now, because I'm probably going to spend more time with the witness on the next document. One or two minutes are not going to be enough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We will come back at quarter past 11.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, we broke off when we were talking about General Alagic. Would you agree that in your book you described one -- the one and only time that you met him?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall specifically, because it's a book numbering 1.000 pages.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Do you remember describing a meeting like that that you talked about yesterday?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did describe a meeting with him.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, I have been asked by the Trial Chamber and the interpreters that we make a pause between my question and your answer because we're speaking the same language. Do you understand me?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: When I finished my question, please would you just pause before you begin answering?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like you to look at document D333. This is again an excerpt from your book about the meeting with Alagic, and I would like to show them to you. First, Witness, I would like you to look at page 06050552. Actually, can you look at the last sentence at the bottom of the page. Would you agree that here you describe your arrival at Guca Gora? Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would also like to refresh your memory. If you can look at the following page.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I can assist. In the English it's on the first page. The relevant text begins with the words "When I arrived in Guca Gora." This is some 10 lines from the top of the page.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I would like to quote this part of the document. "I thought that your commander Wahiuddin ..." can you find that?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. "Where is he? I'd like to have a word with him." So here you are describing the conversation between General Alagic, as you said, and Ebu El Sadik. Is this correct? Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that Alagic said, "'Where is he? I'd like to have a word with him.' Ebu El Sadik told him rudely, 'I told you I was in command here. You talk to me if you have something to say.' The General said, 'I've learned about your intentions. You're under my command, and you don't have my permission to destroy the church. The planting of explosives must stop immediately. Our unit will be sent to protect the church.' Ebu El Sadik laughed and then told him with an indescribable lack of courtesy --"

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Lack of courtesy."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: "'We'll stop it, boss, but first of all you have to suck my D.' Then he became serious and continued. 'Who do you think you are to give us orders? We'll do what Allah Jalishanu [phoen] ordered -- ordered us to do. We don't take any orders from anyone but him. We don't be afraid of anyone, not even you. Leave us at once.'" And then a little later you say: "'And do you know who you're talking to? You're wrong if you think we're under your command. We and not you and your army liberated this village, so it will be the way we want and not the way you do.' The General said in a sharp, threatening voice, 'If by any chance you activate the explosive and destroy the church, I will strike at you with my entire corps and kill you all.' Ebu El Sadik gave a loud laugh and said, nodding his head as if his neck hurt, 'Just you try and you'll see how you will drown in your own blood.' Then he stepped up to him and pushed him with his hands, saying, 'Now get the hell out of here as far as you can -- as far as you can before I ripped your -- rip your head off. You've already made my blood pressure rise.'" Witness, did you faithfully describe this incident with Alagic?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Actually, Witness, on that occasion the Mujahedin did not heed General Alagic. What is more, they threatened to kill him; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: They even physically assaulted him; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: On that occasion they actually listened to Wahiuddin, and I'm going to put it to you why if you accept that. Now I would just like you to look at the same page. It's towards the bottom of the page. You are explaining the conversation with Wahiuddin, who said -- or who explained: "I would like to knock down this church. I would also like to raze this church."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Indiscernible].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. This is on page 2, or on the second page. It's line 11, Your Honours, beginning with the words "I would also like to raise this church."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: He, Wahiuddin, said: "I would also like to raise this church to the ground, but we don't do it so as to avoid confusion, possibly even a conflict between us and the Bosniaks. Let them come and take control of this damn church. We don't need it." And now, Witness, just to ask you this, did you faithfully describe this part of the conversation as well?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Actually, Witness, your Mujahedin chief, Wahiuddin, estimated that at that point it was not in his interest to have a conflict with the Bosniaks and that was why he ordered you not to destroy the church. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you actually listened to him and not to Alagic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can this document please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 332.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to draw the witness's attention again to the interview that we looked at in Der Spiegel. This was D319 -- or, rather, Exhibit 326. Your Honours, it's in the first binder that I provided yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I would just like to draw your attention to one sentence in this interview, which is just beneath the lines "Lights with a chain-saw." You said: "'No general could command us,' former al-Qaeda activist Ali Hamad said about his time as the commander of the Mujahedin unit in town." I would just like to ask you, is it correct that you stated this to Der Spiegel?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now I would like to put some more questions to you, a few questions about the 7th Muslim Brigade that you testified about yesterday to make things quite clear. You said that you at no point in time were a member of the 7th Muslim Brigade; is that correct? You yourself.

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also said that you didn't know its structure. You were not familiar with its structure.

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I would like to ask you something. Would you agree that Bosniaks, local fighters that you met there, were not very familiar with military skills at the time that you testified about? This was 1992 and the first half of 1993. That they were not as skilled as you, the foreign Mujahedin. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Local Muslims never trained foreign fighters. Would you agree?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, you didn't know of any example of local Muslims training the Mujahedin in military skills or combat skills when they came to Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, can we look at D334, Witness, please. Witness, the Prosecutor showed you two documents yesterday which were admitted which refer to the guerrilla. I would like us to look at the documents. The document is D334, an order of the 7th Muslim Brigade of the 18th of February, 1993, and it refers to the training of the guerrilla group Mountain Forest. Witness, can you please look at the order which states in paragraph 1: "Train the guerrilla group Mountain Forest according to the existing plan and schedule." Witness, you agreed that Bosnian did not train the Mujahedin; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I didn't know cases like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Very well. You stayed in Bosnia, especially in that initial period. Would you agree that the Bosnians had very strange names for their units, the Swans, the Wolves, ducks, and geese, and so on and so forth?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that it's not unusual that they would name a part of their unit mountain or forest? Would you consider that unusual for a guerrilla group to do that?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. So you cannot rule out the possibility that what they term here as a guerrilla group Mountain Forest is just a normal part of their unit?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not really familiar with that, but I did say that such a name did exist.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. That's a fair answer. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can this document be given an exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just -- let me just get a slight explanation. I keep hearing from the interpretation the word "forest," not "guerrilla Mountain Forest." I don't see it, the word "forest," on the document. Could I be corrected to it, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, perhaps the document can be placed on the ELMO. Then in line one of the order it says: "Train the guerrilla group," and then in quotes: "'Planina-Suma,' according to the existing plan and programme." In the English text it also says: "Train the 'Planina-Suma'," those are Bosnian words, "guerrilla group." The first line in the English version, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 333.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I would like to draw your attention again to a part of your testimony from yesterday in response to the Prosecutor's questions about the 7th Muslim Brigade and speaking about -- and you also talked about this in your statement of the 15th of August, 2006. Yesterday you used the following words, I'm going to read them back to you, you said: "Guerrilla was part of the 7th Muslim Brigade." What did you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I meant the Turkish guerrilla, and that they were part of the 7th Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Just to clarify what the words "Usus davu [phoen]," "part of," what do they mean?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: That they were part of the same brigade. They were included in the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if the witness can now look at document D336, for the transcript. It's a part of the statement to the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would just like to refresh your recollection, Witness, about the statement you provided to the Prosecutor in August 2006.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm going to look at page 82 of the transcript. The accused has it, and I think that you also have it. Your Honours, the last two lines are relevant, and then that goes on to the following page.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you see that in the transcript? Witness, in the Bosnian it's on the second page, the part that I'm interested in. I'm going to quote it to you. You said: "Yes, but the 7th Muslim Brigade was composed of local combat amounts, but it had very close cooperation with foreign Mujahedin." So for a certain period of time Mujahedin occupied several large premises which were part of the premises of the 7th Muslim Brigade. And the investigator put a question to you: "But they were not under their command." And then you replied: "No. It was only cooperation." Please, so in your statement to the investigators do you agree that you said that the Mujahedin were not under the command of the 7th Muslim? Is this correct.

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: That is correct. And this part of the statement that I read back to you, is that correct, the statement that you provided to the investigators?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. But I was thinking of the Mujahedin who were under the command of the Muslim forces in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you were not thinking of the 7th Muslim Brigade, but you were thinking of the Muslim forces in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. What I want to say, when I deny that the Mujahedin were under the command of the Muslim 7 forces, I was not thinking of the guerrilla, but I was thinking of the Mujahedin forces that were in Travnik within the Muslim forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So how do you explain this part of the testimony or the statement? You said: "The 7th Muslim was composed of local combatants." Please, how would the Turkish guerrilla then be part of the local combatants?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I confirmed that yesterday, because -- for two reasons. The first one was that because during my visit to the facilities where the 7th Muslim was located, I met some of those Turks who were in the guerrilla, and then the attack on Ilijas in 1992. During that attack I saw a group of Turks, Turkish guerrillas, who participated in the war under the command of the 7th Muslim. So I confirm that on the basis of that, that they were part of the 7th Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right, Witness. Just to clarify the following: You, based on the fact that you saw some people from the Turkish guerrilla in the -- at the premises of the 7th Muslim, you base the conclusion that they were part of that force. Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, you have no other proof for that? And I will go back to that.

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have other proof other than what I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. And before we talked about the participation, about the fighting in Visegrad, the Visegrad-Ilijas elevation, that's what you called it, would you agree that I showed you an excerpt showing that the Arabs left with -- without the command of Ramo Durmis, and you confirmed that the Arabs at the time had their own command. They were not reporting to Ramo Durmis, but they listened to their own Mujahedin command.

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well, then. How were they under the command of the 7th Brigade? The fact that they fought together, do you consider that to mean that they were under their command?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I meet fighters from the 7th Muslim Brigade. They were local people, and among them there were Turks. So the 27 of us foreign Mujahedin that were there and the Turkish guerrillas, there was a misunderstanding and we exchanged fire. We shot at them, and they fire at us. And then the local people from the 7th Brigade said that they were their people and that they had come to the 7th Brigade. So on that basis you come to the conclusion that the 7th was the command of these people.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Witness, do you agree that you, yesterday during your testimony, described an incident between the 7th Muslim Brigade and the Mujahedin when members of the 7th Muslim Brigade killed two Mujahedin? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And in this connection I should like the witness to have a look at D338, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... D338. What shall we do with D336?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. May the document be given an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: D336 is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 334.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you described for us yesterday a serious misunderstanding incident between the 7th Muslim Brigade and the Mujahedin, and I would like you to look at this document D338, and I draw your attention to page 2, paragraph 13. It's the same in English. At paragraph 13, Witness. In this paragraph 13 of this document of the 7th Muslim Brigade I will quote: "Urgently sort out matters with all armed formations that have not been brought under the command of the BH army. As regards HVO units, they are a component of the armed forces and full cooperation must be established with them. Instructions will follow on how to carry out further organisation." Witness, please, on the basis of this document we see that the commander of the 7th Muslim Brigade is ordering that matters be sorted out with armed formations that are not under the command of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina and which are not the HVO either. That is what the document says. Would you allow for the possibility that here he is referring to the Mujahedin, that is sorting out matters with the Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you mean the Mujahedin coming from Travnik, I exclude that possibility because the 7th Muslim had no right to make any decisions about them.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I'm not talking about the Mujahedin from Travnik. I'm talking about the Mujahedin in general, about formations that are not under the control of the army and are not the HVO. Would you allow for that possibility? You have described a serious conflict when there was shooting between the 7th Muslim and the Mujahedin regarding the killing of Efendija Karalic. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you then allow for the possibility?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. That is a fair reply.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, can this document be given an Exhibit number, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 335.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have confirmed for us that the Mujahedin wanted to kill Efendija Mahmut Karalic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that in your book you described that they wanted to kill Ademovic as well? Is that right too?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me now move on to another segment having -- which you also testified about yesterday. In your statement you said that you received food, uniforms, and weapons from the Muslim forces; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I wish to remind you and to refresh your memory in connection with a part of the statement that you gave to the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness have a look at D344, 344. Is it, Your Honour, the last sentence on page 55, and it goes on on page 56. That is the relevant portion.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have in the translation the part where the investigator is asking you whether you receive any kind of salary, and the investigator asked you whether you received any financial support.

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. In fact, we gave then money, because in those days they had no money, so they couldn't even pay their own soldiers let alone pay us.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, is that a true description with respect to the local fighters?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
