Your answer was that you were a member before the El Mujahid Detachment was formed. Did I hear you correctly?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: My question to you is: After it was formed, did you ever become a member?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not a member of the detachment, but Zubeir's unit and the Mujahedin Detachment were cooperating.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let me ask you for clarification about a point that you discussed. Yesterday you were shown a clip of the church in Guca Gora with people, soldiers, inside. Remember that?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And I just want to confirm with you that am I right that I heard you say yesterday that the condition in which that church was as it was being shown in the clip, it was before it was destroyed?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, today you were asked a question by Judge Lattanzi, and in her question she mentioned that the general who stopped the destruction of that church succeeded. I'm not quite clear. Was the church successfully saved from destruction or was the church destroyed?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was saved from -- or spared from destruction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So when you said yesterday that you were seeing the church on the clip was before its destruction, what did you mean?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I meant that it was from the inside, the furniture. When I saw it the church was neat. And also in the footage that was shown to me by Mr. Mundis was neat. After that, the church was destroyed from the inside. I'm thinking about the objects and the furniture that was inside the church. When I say that the church was spared from destruction after the conversation with Mehmed Alagic, it means that it was spared from being blown up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The building was spared. That's what you meant.

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, just had building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That explains it. Today you -- I don't know whether this is maybe an interpretation matter, but I heard in the interpretation that -- a word called Taguts was used. I just wanted to find out what Taguts are.

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The Tagud [phoen] rules referred to any rules that are not in keeping with Islamic rules. Actually, what is being said is that they would only respect Islamic rules, regardless of whether it was in conditions of war or not. As for the other rules, even though they may be valid, they would not be accepted and would -- would not wish to know about them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You told us that you were tried for allegedly saving people and ordering your soldiers not to kill prisoners of war, and other things. Are you aware of any other soldiers in the El Mujahedin who were prosecuted by the El Mujahid court for any crimes or irregularities that they may have committed?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know only about the case of Iraqi Abduladim Maqtouf. He was sentenced before the state court. I don't recall exactly whether it was in 2005. But in any case, I think that the court did not reach a real decision or proper decision about him, because this was a person who was not guilty. From 2003, I gave several statements about the crime for which Abduladim Maqtouf was convicted. So they did not convict the person who actually perpetrated the crime. They convicted the person who had nothing to do with the crime.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sure, but that was a state court. It was not an El Mujahid court, an al-Qaeda court.

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes. Excuse me. Then I misunderstood what you said. You're thinking about al-Qaeda and its courts. I think that there were several other men who were detained. In al-Qaeda rules, any soldier who belongs to al-Qaeda, and even if he does not belong to al-Qaeda but is among al-Qaeda people, if he does something that does not suit them, they would punish him. If he does something major that al-Qaeda could not overlook, then he would have to be executed. I know that there were two or three other people who were detained, imprisoned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: During the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, during the war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. And very briefly, are you able to tell us what they were accused of having committed?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know myself specifically what.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I still have a few questions. I realise we have gone beyond quarter past. I'm not quite sure how long the questions from the counsel is going -- are going to be. Is it possible that we could go on for a little long while -- a little while longer, or shall we adjourn to tomorrow? Are you likely to be long?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I believe the Prosecution will have anywhere from three to five questions, which hopefully if we can get brief answers to shouldn't take too long.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Same applies to me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'll ask that the interpreters please bear with us. Maybe we might just finish today. You said you were sentenced to 20 days imprisonment for what you were tried for by the al-Qaeda court. Were you in prison for 20 days?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I spent a bit longer there. Maybe 27 days. I was not freed from prison, actually. I escaped.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. I would like to clear one other point. This is my last point that I would like to clear. In the questions that were put to you by Judge Harhoff, I heard you say that if -- if there were 300 or even a thousand El Mujahid -- Mujahedin soldiers, the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina should and could have been able to prevent them or to publish them or to contain their crimes. Did I hear you correctly to say that?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But I also heard you say, for instance, that the military police could not -- and this may be a question of interpretation. What I heard was could not do anything with crimes that were being committed, and you gave as one of the examples the soldier who confiscated a car, and you said 50 police went to his house and they could not do anything. Is it that they could not do anything, or was it because they didn't want to do anything?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I said that the B and H army was able to prevent the Mujahedin from doing what will they did during the war, I always am thinking about the high-ranking officers. I'm thinking of the political and military leadership. When I mention police or military police, that they couldn't do anything in relation to the Mujahedin, I said that the police seemed not to have the authority to do anything against the Mujahedin. And what I meant to say by that is that those who were in the military leadership did not allow the police to do its work in relation to the Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That concludes my questions. Any questions arising from the questions by the Bench? Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Just a few.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: In response to a question from the Presiding Judge, you indicated that there may have been a small number of other cases heard before the Mujahedin court or courts, and my question to you, sir, is do you recall the approximate time period of those other small number of cases that you were aware of?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, you also mentioned in response to a question by Judge Harhoff several times in explaining an answer an individual named Sead Brkic. Can you tell us, sir, what unit Sead Brkic commanded?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not Sead Brkic but Sead Urkic. Sead Urkic, or from what he told me, was a major, and he was heading a special unit in the 3rd Corps. He was close to General Sakib Mahmuljin. And his unit always participated in the attacks in which we participated, the Zubeir unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And this instance where you saw these two trucks at a check-point, do you recall approximately when that was?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which area are you thinking? Are you thinking of the time maybe, if it was light or dark or -- what are you thinking of exactly?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If you can give us the approximate day or month or year when -- when you were at this check-point where you saw these two trucks.

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was in 1995, and I really do not remember the date, the month, but I think that it was before the end of 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And would it help had you, sir, if you could put it into the context of any military operations that you may have been involved in in 1995? Was it before any combat operation that you remember, or after any particular combat operation?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was after the Paljenik and Gradic locations were captured. The whole Vozuca was occupied then.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Hamed, in response to a question from Judge Harhoff, you made reference to -- or you were asked about the Geneva Conventions, and I'm just wondering, sir, if at any time when you were a soldier or a fighter in the war in Bosnia if you ever saw a Bosnian language publication called "Instructions to the Muslim Fighter."

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never saw that, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And my final question to you, sir, again in response to it a question from the Bench, you answered that the leaders of the Mujahedin, the foreign Mujahedin, attempted to conceal their links to al-Qaeda, and my question really is, if you know, how many of the foreign Mujahedin were al-Qaeda members? Was it all of them, some of them, a few of them, a majority of them?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was a minority of them. Mostly this refers to people who were in important positions in the Mujahedin forces. And it also refers to a small number of fighters who also participated in the fighting in Afghanistan.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you be more specific, sir, in terms of numbers when you say a small number of people? Can you -- can you be more specific as to how many of the foreign Mujahedin were -- were al-Qaeda members?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not able to specify, because we ourselves as al-Qaeda members cannot easily know about each other unless a common assignment is at hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hamed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mundis. Madam Vidovic. Further cross-examination by Ms. Vidovic:

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I only have a few questions for you. During your testimony, you mentioned seeing a person, Abid Ash Shargi, killing a Serb soldier. Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see it, but I was told by his soldiers that he slit the throat of the Serb after he was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Abid Ash Shargi was actually the deputy of Abu al Zubeir. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me now ask you something about the corpses that you said you saw in the trucks. You remember that?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You don't know whether those people were killed in battle or were captured and then killed. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that those trucks were not something that you saw in the El Mujahid camp or anywhere near it even?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I know that these two trucks were heading towards Zavidovici. I don't know where.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know what the 13th kilometre is?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did you know where the El Mujahedin camp was during this period?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know, but I never went there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know the location roughly?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Will you tell us how far these trucks were from the camp in terms of distance?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume about 15 or so kilometres. I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did I understand you correctly when you mentioned Sead Urkic that you said that he did not take part in that operation?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: He took part as a commander. He was issuing orders to his units from Zavidovic, similar to what Zubeir was doing.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, briefly I have to show this witness a document. 351, please. Your Honours, this is page 2 of the English version in this document, and the relevant passage starts from the fifth line, roughly, of this text.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]... at 351.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that will be the right page. Yes, we see it on the screen now, Your Honour. It is the fifth line from the top, and it starts with the words "My superior ordered this."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]... screen is not the same document as we have at 351 in our file.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, Your Honour. It's 353. I asked for 353. This is the English translation of that document, the one we see on the ELMO. It may be an interpretation error.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, will you please read this. Do you agree, Witness, that you're telling us here about the conversation that you had with Mr. Urkic?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me quote for you. You said: "My superior ordered this, and I wouldn't listen to anyone but him. 'You have to go into attack immediately.' Because of these words of his I felt insulted, so I decided to respond in the same measure and said I understood but, 'I wouldn't take orders from you or from your Sakib, nor from anyone but from Abu Zubeir.'" You go on and call Sakib and tell him there will be no attack without the presence of the medical unit. So let me ask you once again. Didn't you show here your relationship towards the army?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You were not listening to orders from the army on any occasion.

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: We need to know the circumstances under which these words were uttered.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: My question is is this true, and the witness says yes. Witness, you spoke to us today about the authorities of Bosnia-Herzegovina and their reaction and you mentioned immunity, but in fact, you know nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was just -- I was just thanking you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So you're just speculating, aren't you? You're not aware of these facts. You were not present at such meetings.

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are not right. If I didn't know what was going on during the war, I certainly wouldn't be here. If I didn't know what was happening during the war, the American FBI would not come to talk to me. If I don't know anything, it's best for me to leave immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, please. Were you present at any meeting at which immunity for the Mujahedin was discussed?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you about my conclusions on the basis of everything that was happening. So if I am mistaken, if I do something wrong and nobody punishes me, it means that someone is protecting me. I myself don't know who that is. I would like to know who was responsible for this, because we did all we did and without any punishment. I didn't name anyone. I didn't say such-and-such a person was at fault. I just said that somebody was protecting us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: One more question. You told Their Honours why you were taken to the military court and why you were punished.

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: But you didn't tell us the whole truth, did you?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm -- if I'm answering one question, do I need to repeat half of what I wrote in my book? Of course I try to answer questions as briefly as possible. I know Their Honours have copies of my book. If you need more information about a particular event, why don't you look it up in my book?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me ask you just one more question in this connection. Actually, you were put on trial, among other things there, because you had assaulted a young girl and had sexual intercourse with her, and that is what Dr. Abu Haris reprimanded you for.

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not true, and I explained this in my book. If this was so, I wouldn't have mentioned it in my book. Why am I revealing this in my book? I see that you are not aware of what went on during the war. Forgive me, but I was here from the beginning of the war until the end. Perhaps you spent your time in your own home.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Would you agree that the father of that child reported the event to Dr. Abu Haris?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not true. I don't know what child you're talking about. I did have a girlfriend, but that wasn't a child.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as this is an important issue, D357, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before we go to D357, do you -- what do you want to do with D353?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I apologise. Could this be admitted into evidence, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: D353 is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 347.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: My.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, look at page 06050628. A very small segment somewhere around the middle of this book when you tell -- when you're telling us about the conversation with Abu El Haris during the trial, you say: "He intentionally or unintentionally insulted me when he said that I had an affair as well as sex with a child." That's what I am talking about, Witness.

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I know what I put down in my book. I wrote that text under the heading "I Have Nothing With Amra." And then I went on to explain the real reason for my arrest and to deny that this had happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: In other words, you're telling us that this didn't happen.

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly. That's what I'm trying to explain here.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me ask you another question, Mr. Abdali [phoen], because you are Mr. Abdali. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: ALI AHMAD ALI HAMAD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think you started insulting me. I don't see any reason for you to call me by a name that is not mine, that it doesn't suit me, because you read it in my book. So don't use that name. Please look at my documents and see whether it says Ali or Abdali.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, you were born and you lived and you grew up and came to Bosnia-Herzegovina with the name Abdali instead of Ali Ahmad Hamad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We've gone well beyond the scope of questions put by Your Honours to this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the need has arisen in connection with your questions for me to focus once again on the credibility of this witness, and that is my reasoning. If I may -- I may continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think the need has arisen for you to insult me, and I am no longer prepared to answer questions from the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just a second, Mr. Hamed. Madam Vidovic, the need may have arisen for you to ask questions, but I think you should stay within the questions arising -- you must ask questions arising from the questions asked by the Bench. I'm not quite sure I understand how the line of questioning that you are now undertaking relates to what the questions -- what the Bench asked, unless you are able to explain it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it doesn't stem from your questions, and I will stop my cross-examination there. There are other witnesses. Thank you. I have no more questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Madam Vidovic, what do you want to do with D357?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I would like to tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. This now brings us to the conclusion of -- I beg your pardon. The document 357 is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 348.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Hamed, thank you. Let me just say that this brings us to the conclusion of your testimony in this court. May I, on behalf of the Trial Chamber, thank you for availing yourself to come and testify. I hope you -- you've -- you feel you have made a contribution to the trial here by coming here, and you are now excused. You may stand down. Once again, thank you very much for coming to testify.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We have now come to the conclusion of the proceedings pursuant to Rule 4 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia. We will not be sitting again tomorrow as was anticipated. May the Chamber take this opportunity to gratefully acknowledge the assistance of the Bosnia and Herzegovina State Court, and in particular Ms. Medjita Kreso [phoen], the President of the court; Mr. Tarik Abdulhak [phoen] from Registry; and all other state court officers for enabling a smooth operation of this hearing. While I'm at the point of thanking the state court officials, may I also add that I would like to give Chamber's gratitude to all the people who contributed towards the smooth running of the operation. This includes the security police from Bosnia and Herzegovina and every -- and all other people who were involved. I may not be able to mention them all, but you are all thanked, and thank you so much. That concludes the hearing. Court adjourned.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.44 p.m.
